{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.4,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is declared as value \"24k\", but its own LCSC/MPN fields and description describe a 24 ohm part (MPN FRC0805J240TSD, \"24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor\"). The SPICE deck also models it as 24k.",
      "expected": "A resistor whose value matches its MPN and description. If the intent is a 24 ohm element across the output, it would dissipate far more than an 0805 125 mW part can handle, so the value and sourcing data cannot both be right.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\") ... (description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "Either the bleed/divider between the two output rails has the wrong resistance, or the wrong part was sourced. A 24 ohm part across the output would overheat or load the supply heavily.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60"],
      "pins": ["D30.4", "D30.2", "R60.1", "R60.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "Net-(D30-K2)"],
      "observed": "The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode A2 (pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode K2 (pin 2) goes through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. The LED therefore sits across a single node and cannot conduct.",
      "expected": "The anode of the second LED should be tied to a supply such as +3V3 (as the first LED's anode A1 is tied to LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV), with its cathode driven through R60 to ESTOP_OUT.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"K2\") (pintype \"input\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The E-stop indicator LED channel never lights, and the resistor and LED form a loop on ESTOP_OUT.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D4", "D14", "D23"],
      "pins": ["D4.2", "D14.2", "D23.2"],
      "nets": ["/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW"],
      "observed": "Net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only to the anodes of D4, D14 and D23. No source, switch or jumper drives it, so these LED anodes have no supply.",
      "expected": "A powered supply net for the status LEDs. The name \"POWER_SW\" implies a switched 3.3 V source, which is absent.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"32\") (name \"/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D14\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The PI activity LED (D4) and the Ethernet link/activity LEDs (D14, D23) cannot light.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist and SPICE deck agree and the main power, CAN, USB and E-stop paths look consistent. The strongest candidate is R36, whose value of 24k conflicts with its 24 ohm MPN and description. Two lower-confidence wiring issues are the dead D30 LED channel and the unpowered status-LED net."
}

anomalies.observed: R36 is declared as value "24k", but its own LCSC/MPN fields and description describe a 24 ohm part (MPN FRC0805J240TSD, "24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor"). The SPICE deck also models it as 24k.
anomalies.expected: A resistor whose value matches its MPN and description. If the intent is a 24 ohm element across the output, it would dissipate far more than an 0805 125 mW part can handle, so the value and sourcing data cannot both be right.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R36") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: Either the bleed/divider between the two output rails has the wrong resistance, or the wrong part was sourced. A 24 ohm part across the output would overheat or load the supply heavily.

anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode A2 (pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode K2 (pin 2) goes through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. The LED therefore sits across a single node and cannot conduct.
anomalies.expected: The anode of the second LED should be tied to a supply such as +3V3 (as the first LED's anode A1 is tied to LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV), with its cathode driven through R60 to ESTOP_OUT.
anomalies.impact: The E-stop indicator LED channel never lights, and the resistor and LED form a loop on ESTOP_OUT.

anomalies.observed: Net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only to the anodes of D4, D14 and D23. No source, switch or jumper drives it, so these LED anodes have no supply.
anomalies.expected: A powered supply net for the status LEDs. The name "POWER_SW" implies a switched 3.3 V source, which is absent.
anomalies.impact: The PI activity LED (D4) and the Ethernet link/activity LEDs (D14, D23) cannot light.
